items.problem: Multi-scenario SDK-sample shell: NavigationView highlights but content Frame never switches; scenarios 2-4 render Scenario 1's UI (dead scenarios). 3 of 4 features fail (score 25/100).
items.evidence: migration-score.json features[1..3] verdict=fail 'nav item highlights but content pane never switches'; MainPage.xaml.cs (build session-log ~2228) set NavView.SelectedItem = Scenarios[0] in ctor and navigated only from NavView_SelectionChanged, citing the anchor.
items.root_cause: The navigationview-frame-wiring anchor recommended a constructor SelectedItem assignment to drive navigation via SelectionChanged. Constructor-time SelectedItem does not reliably raise SelectionChanged, and for MenuItemsSource data items SelectionChanged alone does not reliably drive the Frame, so scenario switching is dead.
items.change: Rewrote the navigationview-frame-wiring anchor to: (1) navigate the first scenario EXPLICITLY on Loaded rather than via a constructor SelectedItem side-effect; (2) use NavigationView.ItemInvoked (fires reliably per click, incl. data-bound items) instead of SelectionChanged-only; (3) strengthen the falsifiable check to require verifying that selecting a SECOND scenario switches the Frame, not just first-scenario render. Updated the SKILL.md shell-mapping row note to match.
items.expected_effect: Migrated multi-scenario shells will switch content on every nav click; scenarios 2..N render their own controls.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, requirements for scenarios 2-4 go fail->pass; UIA tree after selecting scenario 2 contains scenario-2 controls, not scenario-1 controls.

deferred_to_human: Tier-1 idea (out of scope for this loop): extend Test-AppLaunch.ps1 / a Validate step to actually exercise nav switching (select item 2, assert Frame content changed) instead of an alive-only smoke check — the current smoke launch is blind to dead-scenario navigation. This touches migration tooling but should be reviewed by a human before automating UI-driving in the smoke step.
